items.title: Charlie De Vore Interview, 1962-07-04
items.q: The interviewee discusses 'Ori's band' and Ori's musicianship in the third person ('Ori was a damn good trombone player', 'tough guy to work for though, from all the reports that I've heard'), indicating knowledge of Ori as a bandleader but no direct personal interaction or collaboration is stated.

ctx.x: combination of well, the trombone man it's a combination of slide and your chops. Like Jim, when he'll hit a long note he'll go like that and he does that with his lip. But then Louie when he hits something he goes he shakes the slide moves the slide back and forth as fast as he can. And Ori and our trombone player that's how we worked on his vibrato by using the slide. That's how you get that nice tone. See a trombone is the only instrument in the band that can do it that way because he has a slide. Well now do…

involved in tonality though? If we're going to set up some sort of little school or something do you think how do you think we should start? Do you think we should start with individual lessons from an old musician to a young guy or should it be the band or what or both or everything? Well the way I see it
